plans: Reproduce-then-boundary-containment: first reproduce the flaw against a live local handler using a fixture root with a sibling marker file and raw requests carrying literal parent-directory segments, so no client-side normalization hides the behavior. Characterize which shapes leak, including the extensionless index-append branch and deep traversal. Then implement the minimal repair at the path-derivation boundary: after joining, resolve the configured root and the joined target and accept only when the target equals the root or begins with the root plus the path separator; otherwise return the existing 404 page. Close with a regression suite covering ordinary files, nested files, directory index, missing files, and traversal variants. Assumption: the join is the single trust boundary; falsifier: a leaking shape that a resolved-prefix check still admits.

Input-normalization/decoding-discipline: treat URL interpretation as the trust boundary. First map what URL parsing yields for literal parent segments, percent-encoded dot segments, doubled slashes, and mixed-separator variants in the local runtime. Then repair by normalizing the pathname before the join: collapse dot segments and reject or strip disallowed characters, then join with the root. Verify that every previously leaking encoding variant returns 404 while ordinary relative paths still resolve. Assumption: all leaks reduce to pathname content; falsifier: a non-dot-segment input that still escapes, or a normal path that normalization breaks.

Read-time realpath sandbox: treat the filesystem read as the trust boundary. Keep the existing path derivation, but before the regular-file check and the stream, resolve both the root and the target with a realpath call and require the resolved target to be inside the resolved root, rejecting with the existing 404 page otherwise. Add a fixture symlink inside the root pointing outside to test symlink escape, alongside the traversal regression suite. Assumption: string-level derivation may remain as-is if the read is sandboxed; falsifier: a target whose realpath escapes while its string form looks contained, or a legitimate in-root file that starts returning 404.
